summary.one_liner: LavaSR is a lightweight Python speech enhancement and bandwidth-extension model that upsamples low-quality, noisy speech (8–48 kHz input) into clean 48 kHz audio.
summary.what_it_does: LavaSR takes low-sample-rate or noisy speech and produces cleaner 48 kHz output. It adapts the Vocos architecture for bandwidth extension (audio upsampling) and adds a Linkwitz-Riley-inspired refiner to improve quality. The README says it accepts any input sample rate from 8 kHz to 48 kHz. It has an optional denoise flag for audio with noise, and a batch flag for very long audio. Usage is through a Python API: load a model with LavaEnhance2, call load_audio and enhance, then save with soundfile. The README claims about 5000x realtime on GPU, over 60x realtime on CPU, and roughly 500 MB VRAM. It also lists community ports (ComfyUI node, GUI app, C++, ONNX).
use_cases: On-device enhancement of calls or audio
how_to_run: uv pip install git+ (URL truncated in README)
notable: Vocos-based single-pass architecture, which the README credits for its speed
Accepts any input sampling rate from 8 kHz to 48 kHz
Reported model size around 50 MB, far smaller than diffusion-based alternatives in its comparison table
Trained from a Vocos prior with 50k steps on VCTK, using random resampling and added noise
Community ports including ComfyUI node, C++, and ONNX
caveats: The install command in the README is truncated ("uv pip install git+") so the exact URL is missing
Speed and quality figures are the author's, measured on an A100 GPU and VCTK validation
Training code and music/general-audio models are listed as not yet released on the roadmap
Lowering the cutoff can improve quality but may sound metallic, per the README
keywords: low quality audio to high quality
